title: Residency retention & erasure SLA matrix
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a cross-functional working doc to propose a minimal, product-mapped retention + erasure + evidence SLA matrix for region-pinned customers. Goal is to produce a pragmatic implementation surface that legal, sales, and engineering can agree on for initial GA of residency entitlements (hosted + dedicated + private).

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Customers demand clear guarantees about how long user data, request logs, and ephemeral caches are retained in a pinned region, and how quickly we can complete a verified erasure request.
- Current residency work focuses on routing and storage locality but lacks a standardized timeline and evidence package for erasure/retention across tiers. That gap slows legal signoff and lengthens sales cycles.

Assumptions and constraints:
- "Pinned region" means requests and telemetry tied to a tenant are anchored to resources physically or logically inside the selected territory for the retention window.
- We distinguish three logical artifact classes: "User Payloads" (customer-submitted content), "Inference Artifacts" (model inputs/outputs, intermediate KV cache entries), "Operational Logs & Billing" (stack traces, scheduler logs, cost telemetry).
- Implementation must be achievable without complete rewrites of the serving runtime; prefer config-driven enforcement, TTL controls on storage backends, and an erasure orchestration job.
- Evidence package needs to be auditable and minimally invasive (avoid releasing customer data).

Proposed SLA matrix (core proposal):
Columns: Product tier | User Payload retention | Inference Artifacts retention | Operational Logs retention | Max verified erasure time | Evidence included
- Free / Dev: 30 days | 7 days | 90 days | 14 calendar days | timestamped deletion record + region routing log snippet
- Standard / Pro: 12 months | 30 days | 180 days | 7 calendar days | deletion record + object store audit log + operator nonce
- Enterprise (contracted residency): configurable up to 7 years | configurable per contract | 1 year (default, negotiable) | 72 hours (target) | deletion record + signed checksum of erased object identifiers + routing attach logs + KMS audit trail (if used)

Notes on definitions and edge cases:
- "Erasure time" is the maximum time to produce an auditable confirmation that all live copies in the pinned region were removed (not including cold backups kept for legal holds).
- Cold backups / long-term archives are by default excluded unless the customer purchased an archival retention product. For Enterprise, archival retention rules must be explicitly stated in the contract with a legal hold override process.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments: erasure applies to tenant-managed storage connectors as well — we ship a checklist + orchestration API to coordinate erasure across connectors.

Implementation considerations (engineering):
1) Storage TTLs and lifecycle rules: map retention buckets to object prefixes / tags in S3-like stores. Provide automated lifecycle jobs to expire objects.
2) Index & evidence surface: maintain a per-tenant index of object identifiers (hashes, paths) and the region tag. When an erasure request is processed, we mark the index entry as "erased" and include signed metadata (operator id, timestamp).
3) KV / cache eviction: design an idempotent eviction job that can sweep prefix-based KV caches (redis, local SSD) and report counts. For in-flight KV fragments, provide operator-safe draining windows (e.g., quiesce connections, re-route).
4) Telemetry and logging: separate region-tagged operational logs from global control-plane logs. Provide a way to purge region-tagged logs per tenant.
5) API surface: extend tenant management API with endpoints: POST /tenants/{id}/erasure-request , GET /tenants/{id}/erasure-status , GET /tenants/{id}/erasure-evidence.

Evidence package contents (minimal):
- high-level deletion summary (human readable) with timestamps
- list of erased identifiers (object keys, KV keys) as checksums (avoid including plaintext customer payload)
- storage-level audit log lines (or filtered extracts) showing delete operations and region tag
- operator signature (username + id) and system signature (service account)
- optional: KMS logs showing key rotations/destroy commands if keys were rotated as part of erasure

Telemetry & SLOs to monitor:
- Mean time to evidence (MTTE): time from request to evidence bundle ready (goal: enterprise <=72h)
- Erasure success rate: percent of objects marked erased vs objects discovered (goal >= 99.5%)
- Reconciliation lag: time between lifecycle rule expiry and actual index state change (goal < 24h)
- Escalation rate: fraction of erasure requests requiring manual operator intervention (goal <1% for Standard, <0.1% for Enterprise)

Security and compliance notes:
- Evidence bundles must protect customer data — include hashes instead of raw content. Legal may request raw content under subpoena; handle via legal path.
- For regions with stricter laws (e.g., special EU national rules), default timelines might need to be shortened or lengthened per legal opinion — include regional overrides table in contract templates.

Operational playbook (high level):
- Intake: sales/legal records erasure terms in contract metadata and turns on corresponding product entitlement flags (retention TTLs).
- Trigger: customer or admin files erasure request via tenant API or support ticket. System creates a request ticket, schedules a sweep.
- Automated sweep: lifecycle job runs on object store prefixes, KV eviction triggered, streaming caches flushed.
- Verification: index reconciler runs and generates evidence bundle; automated checks verify counts and checksums.
- Manual review: if automated checks fail, operator runs the "erasure-debug" runbook (links in linked_artifacts).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we include telemetry-level retention (metrics/alert history) in the same SLA, or treat metrics as operational logs? Recommend treating metrics as operational logs with conservative default retention.
- Backups: acceptable to exclude geo-replicated backups from standard erasure unless explicit contractual clause is added. Legal to confirm.
- Pricing: should shorter erasure SLAs or longer retention be priced as add-ons? Sales to propose pricing bands.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Legal: confirm acceptable evidence bundle contents and whether checksums alone suffice for audits (owner: Sofia, due 2024-11-15).
- Product: review matrix and confirm tier mapping (owner: Marcus, due 2024-11-18).
- Eng infra: prototype tenant-index + erasure orchestration job and expose tenant API (owner: Liam, spike due 2024-11-22).
- SRE/Oncall: draft erasure-debug operator playbook and escalate flow (owner: Carla Rivera, due 2024-11-25).

Appendix: quick operator checklist for processing a manual erasure request
- Verify tenant entitlement and contract notes in billing system.
- Kick off erasure job via internal endpoint: /internal/erasure/schedule?tenant={id}&scope=full
- Confirm object store lifecycle job initiated and capture the first delete audit lines.
- Run KV sweep in maintenance window; record counts and attach to evidence bundle.
- Generate evidence bundle, sign with service account, store in audit bucket (region-limited).
- Close ticket and dispatch evidence link to customer contact.

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally pragmatic — we want a small set of enforceable guarantees that can be delivered with lifecycle rules, index reconciliation, and a modest erasure orchestration job. Please flag legal/technical concerns inline in comments.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-06: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-11-12: added evidence package spec (Liam)
- 2024-11-20: tightened enterprise erasure target and action items (Sofia)
